newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee prices stable, ACPC no impact.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee prices stable, ACPC no impact.

text.p: Indonesian Robusta coffee prices were generally stable on Monday from a week ago on limited buying interest, traders said.
The local price was quoted unchanged at 2,600-2,650 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra. The export price edged up to $1,200/tonne from $1,118 last week.
"There's not many beans left and only a few exporters are buying to fulfil contracts," one Lampung trader said. "The price is not likely to go below this level."
Indonesia's coffee year ended last September and coffee production will only begin in earnest early next year.
Traders said a one-day meeting of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) in Costa Rica last Friday had no impact on the market.

The ACPC, whose 14 members including Indonesia account for more than 80 percent of world production, said after the meeting that global consumption was outstripping production and that stocks were not increasing in consumer nations.
"Such meetings are usually talk shops. Whatever was put out (by the ACPC) had no impact here," one trader said.
Some traders estimated Indonesia exported more than 350,000 tonnes of coffee during the 1995/96 (Oct/Sept) crop year.
"My estimate is that exports totalled 355,000 tonnes in 1995/96, bringing production to about 465,000 tonnes," one trader said.
The Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters had forecast 1995/96 crop year production at 420,000 tonnes, up from 320,000 tonnes in the previous crop year when output was hit by bad weather.
The group had forecast exports at 275,000 tonnes in the 1995/96 crop year.
